scraped.scraped_description: Human rights researchers often rely on videos shared online to document war crimes, atrocities, and human rights violations. Manually reviewing these videos is expensive, does not scale, and can cause vicarious trauma. As an increasing number of videos are posted, a new approach is needed to understand these large datasets.

name: VFRAME
tagline: Computer vision for OSINT: detecting illegal munitions and documenting war crimes through AI-powered video analysis
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: Reliance on synthetic data generation quality
Dependency on partnership with Tech 4 Tracing for scaling
awards: Mozilla Foundation award for digital rights and open source technology
policy_outcomes: Evidence generated used in international humanitarian law documentation efforts
Adoption by human rights organizations for war crimes investigation workflows
outcome_methodology: Case study documentation of tool adoption by human rights organizations and war crimes investigators; performance metrics validation through peer-reviewed publication
published_performance_metrics: Up to 99% accuracy at over 400 FPS on single workstation for munition detection
documented_limitations: Synthetic data generation dependent on accurate 3D models
Limited to specific object classes currently trained
jurisdictional_scope: International - applicable to any conflict zone with video documentation
failure_modes: Potential for false positives/negatives in object detection
Vicarious trauma risk remains for human reviewers of flagged content
curation_criteria: Open source contributions reviewed by core team; focus on expanding object detection classes and improving synthetic data generation pipelines
contributor_governance: Community contributions accepted via GitHub; core development team maintains quality control and integration decisions
disparity_tracking: Not explicitly tracked; project focuses on geographic coverage across conflict zones rather than demographic representation
community_ownership: Limited community ownership; primarily research-driven project with partnerships rather than community governance model
controversies: Concerns about potential misuse of munition detection technology for targeting purposes
Debate over synthetic data reliability for legal evidence standards
political_bias_allegations: Allegations of Western-centric focus on Syrian and Ukrainian conflicts; limited deployment in other conflict zones
legal_regulatory_issues: Questions regarding admissibility of AI-generated evidence in international courts; concerns about chain of custody for digitally processed evidence

ai_involvement: Core technology: convolutional neural networks for object detection, semantic segmentation, and image classification trained on synthetic data
